Study coverage

Can we trust the evaluators?

Download labels

Each model is tested against 100 known corruptions and 100 meaning-preserving edits. The acceptance boundary is at least 90% detection and at most 5% false positives. These are evaluator checks, not Symphonia performance results.

Primary comparison

Symphonia versus structured synthesis, paired by independent scenario. Repeated runs are averaged within each scenario. Intervals resample whole scenario maps within policy setting.

What this study measures

Experiment A holds participant judgments fixed to isolate information preservation. Experiment B compares responsive participants under product feedback, exact reference feedback, structured summaries and no peer feedback.

Strict fidelity requires a claim to be present with the right meaning, conditions, panel status and evidential status. Consensus uses 80% of valid ratings in one direction, with at least 80% panel coverage; insufficient evidence is a valid answer, while missing responses are separate. Sensitivity analyses use 70% and 90% thresholds.

Narrative and audit-table results are scored separately. Decision readers see only the narrative, policy options and objective. Greater agreement is not automatically a better result.

Scope and limitations

    Protocol and reproducibility

    Read the supplied protocol · Study specification · Analysis data

    Scenario maps—not individual claims—are the independent units of analysis. The main specification is frozen after pilot validation and sample-size planning. Pilot and main scenarios remain separate. Any unfinished protocol components remain visible in the coverage table.
